title: Persist all SQLite databases to disk (keep split)
description:
Several SQLite databases currently use in-memory storage and lose all state on restart. All four databases must be moved to configurable on-disk paths. The four-way split (core.db, transit.db, reader.db, mail.db) is intentional and must be preserved — do not consolidate.

## Current state

| Database | Owner | Current storage | Problem |
|----------|-------|----------------|---------|
| core.db | core crate | On-disk (transit-configured) | Reader creates its own in-memory copy — not shared with transit |
| transit.db | transit | On-disk | OK |
| reader.db | reader | In-memory SQLite (`file:reader_stores_N?mode=memory`) | Lost on restart |
| mail.db | mail | On-disk | OK |

The reader creates two in-memory pools at startup: one for reader-crate schema (article_numbers, overview) and one for core-crate schema (msgid_map). Both are ephemeral. On restart, all article numbers, overview entries, and message-ID mappings are gone.

## Why keep the split

- Each database is owned by one crate; schema migrations run independently
- transit and reader have different lifetimes and may run on different hosts
- Consolidation would couple independently-versioned migration sets and break the crate boundary
- mail.db holds irreplaceable user state; mixing it with reconstructable caches is an ops hazard

## What needs doing

### reader.db (article numbers + overview)

- Add `[database]` section to reader config:
  ```toml
  [database]
  path      = "/var/lib/usenet-ipfs/reader/reader.db"
  core_path = "/var/lib/usenet-ipfs/reader/core.db"
  ```
- `path`: reader-crate schema (article_numbers, overview, block_cache)
- `core_path`: core-crate schema (msgid_map) — separate file from transit's core.db unless the operator explicitly points both at the same file (supported but not required)
- Replace `make_pool_with_reader_migrations` and `make_pool_with_core_migrations` in `server_stores.rs` with on-disk pool construction using the configured paths
- Enable WAL mode on both pools at startup
- `[database]` section is required; startup fails with a clear error if absent

### Idempotency on restart

The reader currently re-ingests articles from IPFS into a fresh overview on every start (backfill). With a persistent reader.db, backfill must be idempotent:
- `INSERT OR IGNORE` for article_numbers and overview rows (CID is the natural unique key)
- Backfill skips CIDs already present in reader.db rather than re-processing them
- On first run (empty database), full backfill proceeds as today

### core.db sharing (optional operator configuration)

If an operator runs transit and reader on the same host and wants them to share a single msgid_map, they can point both `core_path` fields at the same file. Document this in the runbook. SQLite WAL mode handles concurrent access from two processes safely. This is not the default — by default each daemon has its own core.db.

### WAL mode

All four on-disk databases must have WAL mode enabled at connection time (`PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL`). Add this to the pool setup helper used by all crates. WAL allows concurrent reads during writes, which matters for the newsreader workload.

### Startup checks

- Verify configured directories exist and are writable before running migrations
- Fail fast with a path-specific error message if a database cannot be opened
- Log the resolved absolute path of each database at INFO level on startup

## What does NOT change

- Schema for any of the four databases
- Migration numbering or content
- The mail.db path (already on-disk and correctly configured)
- The four-database split

## Acceptance criteria
- Reader state (article numbers, overview, msgid_map) survives a clean restart without re-backfill
- Backfill after restart processes only CIDs not already in reader.db
- Integration tests that construct ServerStores use a tempdir for all four paths (no in-memory pools in non-unit tests)
- All four databases have WAL mode confirmed via `PRAGMA journal_mode` query in a startup test
- Reader config without `[database]` section fails to parse with a message naming the missing field
